empirical
A four-condition, block-randomized online survey experiment in which respondents read dispatches about a fictional Alaska state senator's resignation (control, innuendo, denial, causal correction) and then rated his favorability and the likelihood he took bribes / resigned because of an investigation. The paper reports this one experiment.

summary
Summary
Respondents read a sequence of news dispatches about a fictional Alaska state senator's sudden resignation. Conditions differed in whether the resignation was left unexplained (control), linked by innuendo to a bribery investigation, followed by a denial backed by a prosecutors' letter, or followed by the denial plus an alternate causal explanation (a new job). After a delay task, respondents rated the senator's favorability and the likelihood of bribery or illegal practices (and, outside the control condition, of resigning because of an investigation).

Summary
Respondents read a sequence of news dispatches about a fictional Alaska state senator's sudden resignation. Conditions differed in whether the resignation was left unexplained (control), linked by innuendo to a bribery investigation, followed by a denial backed by a prosecutors' letter, or followed by the denial plus an alternate causal explanation (a new job).
